nodes.statement_tex: A Lipschitz piece consists of an arbitrary subset $A\subset\R^m$ and a Lipschitz map $f:A\to X$. A set is countably covered by such pieces if it lies in the union of the ranges of a countable family. The domains and the family may be empty. No measurability or finite-measure hypothesis is built into the geometric piece.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The target is a metric space.

nodes.title: Euclidean extension of Lipschitz parametrizations
nodes.statement_tex: Every Lipschitz map \(f:A\to\mathbb R^n\), with \(A\subset\mathbb R^m\), admits a globally defined Lipschitz extension \(\widetilde f:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n\).
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The subset \(A\) is arbitrary, possibly empty. The conclusion requires some finite Lipschitz constant, not necessarily the original one.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.
nodes.note: Reuse extend_pi through finite-dimensional coordinates; no optimal Kirszbraun bound needed.

nodes.title: Cones about affine planes
nodes.statement_tex:
For a linear plane \(V\), put \(Q_V=\mathrm{id}-P_V\) and define
\[
 C(x,V,\alpha)=\{y:\|Q_V(y-x)\|\leq\alpha\|P_V(y-x)\|\}.
\]
Geometric applications use \(\alpha\geq0\).
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Work in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space; \(V\) is a linear subspace.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Hausdorff measure on planes
nodes.statement_tex:
For the inclusion \(\iota_V:V\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^n\),
\[
 (\iota_V)_\#\mathcal H_V^m=\mathcal H_{\mathbb R^n}^m\!\restriction V.
\]
This measure is a positive finite scalar multiple of the induced Haar measure. In particular its ball masses scale as \(r^m\); when \(m>0\), spheres have zero mass.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The linear subspace \(V\subset\mathbb R^n\) has dimension \(m\). Intrinsic and ambient Hausdorff measures use the same diameter convention.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.
nodes.note: Split normalization, finiteness, and sphere-null corollaries; do not import tangent or uniform-measure theory.

nodes.title: A plane avoiding an inner cylinder has a small projected direction
nodes.statement_tex:
If \(\|P_Vz-p\|=\rho\) and
\[
 (z+W)\cap B_r(z)\cap\{q:\|P_Vq-p\|<\rho/4\}=\varnothing,
\]
then some unit \(w\in W\) satisfies \(\|P_Vw\|\leq C\rho/r\).
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The planes \(V,W\) have the same positive finite dimension, \(p\in V\), and \(r,\rho>0\) with \(r\) sufficiently larger than \(\rho\). No measure hypothesis is used.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Flat measures
nodes.statement_tex: A measure is $m$-flat if it equals $c\,\mathcal H^m\!\restriction V$ for an $m$-dimensional linear plane $V$ and a positive finite scalar $c$.

nodes.title: Nonnegative compactly supported flatness energy
nodes.statement_tex: For a compactly supported continuous cutoff $\phi$ and a measure $\mu$, set $E_\phi(\mu,V)=\int\phi(z)\operatorname{dist}(z,V)^2\,d\mu$ and $F_\phi(\mu)=\inf_{\dim V=m}E_\phi(\mu,V)$. The data definition is total. Positivity, attainment and continuity theorems impose $m\leq n$, local finiteness, and the relevant cutoff hypotheses.
nodes.proof_tex:
Choose $\phi\in C_c(\mathbb R^n)$ with $0\leq\phi\leq1$,
$\phi=1$ on $\overline B(0,1)$ and support in $B(0,2)$.
Define $F(\mu)=\min_V\int\phi(z)\operatorname{dist}(z,V)^2\,d\mu$.
The minimum is attained. S01 and C01 imply sequential continuity for vague
convergence; S02 implies continuity of $r\mapsto F(D^m_{x,r}\mu)$ for $r>0$.
Flat measures have $F=0$. For a unit uniform measure, $F\leq\varepsilon$
implies that some plane has unit-ball energy at most $\varepsilon$.
nodes.source: De Lellis Lemma 6.20 and Section 6.4, pp.66-69.

nodes.title: Rectifiable sets and measures
nodes.statement_tex: A set $S$ is countably $m$-rectifiable if $\mathcal H^m(S\setminus T)=0$ for a countably Lipschitz-piece-covered set $T$. A measure is $m$-rectifiable if $\mu\ll\mathcal H^m$ and is concentrated on a countably $m$-rectifiable set. Local finiteness, measurability of carriers, and finite Hausdorff mass are separate theorem hypotheses. Absolute continuity absorbs the Hausdorff-null remainder.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Use the Borel measurable structure on the metric target.

nodes.title: Unit ball-law normalization adapter
nodes.statement_tex: For $m>0$, the pure unit-uniform ball law is equivalent to FormalizingGMT's $m$-uniform predicate together with origin support membership and unit closed-ball mass.

nodes.title: Conical measures
nodes.statement_tex: A measure is $m$-conical if $D^m_{0,r}\nu=\nu$ for every $r>0$.

nodes.title: Gaussian moments of a normalized flat measure
nodes.statement_tex: For $\sigma_V$ and $j\geq0$, its Gaussian moment form satisfies $b_{2j,s}(x^{2j})=s^j|P_Vx|^{2j}/j!$, and its odd moments are zero. Equivalently the one-dimensional standard Gaussian even moment is $(2j)!/(2^j j!)$.
nodes.proof_tex:
For every $j\geq1$, $b_{2j}^{(j)}(x^{2j})=|Px|^{2j}$ for every $x$.
Use M02, M03 and the Gaussian moment formula of the flat limit, including the
factorial from M08.
nodes.source: De Lellis Proposition 9.1, Lemmas 9.2,9.4,9.9,9.10 and Proposition 9.5, pp.95-109.

nodes.title: Pure unrectifiability
nodes.statement_tex:
A set \(E\) is purely \(m\)-unrectifiable if
\[
 \mathcal H^m(E\cap R)=0
 \quad\text{for every countably \(m\)-rectifiable set }R.
\]
This canonical definition implies the graph-test version used in the source.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Neither finite measure nor Borel measurability is built into the definition.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.
nodes.note: Use this canonical stronger formulation so core decomposition does not need the image-to-graph theorem; source graph-only equivalence is a companion result.

Define $F(\mu)=\min_V\int\phi(z)\operatorname{dist}(z,V)^2\,d\mu$.

convergence; S02 implies continuity of $r\mapsto F(D^m_{x,r}\mu)$ for $r>0$.
Flat measures have $F=0$. For a unit uniform measure, $F\leq\varepsilon$
implies that some plane has unit-ball energy at most $\varepsilon$.

nodes.title: Density-to-tangent adapters
nodes.statement_tex: For $m>0$, positive finite existing density almost everywhere implies that almost everywhere all tangent measures are $m$-uniform and contain the origin in their support.

nodes.title: Small Gaussian distance energy forces plane support proximity
nodes.statement_tex:
For every $\delta>0$ there exists $\eta>0$ such that if $\nu\in\mathcal U_m$
and $V$ is an $m$-plane with Gaussian distance energy at most $\eta$, every
$x\in V\cap\overline B(0,1)$ has distance less than $\delta$ to the support.
Otherwise rotate planes to one fixed plane, take a convergent subsequence of
measures and alleged holes, and use S04--S05. Vanishing energy puts the limit's
support in the plane; the plane-supported uniform classification identifies it
with $\sigma_V$, contradicting the persistent hole. This lemma does not
require conicality or eigenvalue assumptions.

nodes.statement_tex:
Conicality gives $b_{k,s}=s^{k/2}b_{k,1}$. Comparing with M07 makes odd forms
zero and gives $b_{2j,s}=s^j b_{2j}^{(j)}/j!$.
The support identities give $b_{2j}^{(j)}(x^{2j})=|x|^{2j}$ on the support.

nodes.title: All Gaussian polynomial moments of blow-downs have limits
nodes.statement_tex: For $\nu\in\mathcal U_m$ and every polynomial $P$, the limit of $\int P(z)e^{-|z|^2}\,d(D^m_{0,r}\nu)$ exists as $r\to\infty$. Degree $2j$ moment forms are determined by $b_{2j}^{(j)}/j!$, and odd-degree moments vanish.
nodes.proof_tex:
For odd $k$, $s^{-k/2}b_{k,s}\to0$; for $k=2j$,
$s^{-j}b_{2j,s}\to b_{2j}^{(j)}/j!$.
The factorial is essential; the displayed summary on printed page 74 omits it,
whereas the calculation in Chapter 9 includes it correctly.
Use M03 with $s=r^{-2}$ to deduce the limit of every Gaussian-weighted
polynomial moment of $D^m_{0,r}\nu$ as $r\to\infty$.
nodes.source: De Lellis Lemma 7.2, Definition 7.4, Lemma 7.6, Proposition 7.7, pp.70-84.

The trace calculation is the radial Gaussian second moment. This statement
does not require spectral choices.

nodes.title: Graph parametrization is Lipschitz and antilipschitz
nodes.statement_tex:
If \(f:V\to V^\perp\) is Lipschitz, then \(F(v)=v+f(v)\) is Lipschitz and satisfies
\[
 \|u-v\|\leq\|F(u)-F(v)\|,\qquad P_V(F(v))=v.
\]
Thus \(F\) is injective and its inverse on its range is \(1\)-Lipschitz.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The subspace \(V\) is finite-dimensional. A finite Lipschitz bound for \(f\) is given; an optimal bound for \(F\) is unnecessary.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Pairwise cone condition implies graph containment
nodes.statement_tex:
If \(y\in C(x,V,\alpha)\) for every \(x,y\in F\), then there is a Lipschitz \(f:V\to V^\perp\) such that
\[
 F\subset\{v+f(v):v\in V\}.
\]
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The set \(F\subset\mathbb R^n\) is arbitrary, \(V\) is an \(m\)-plane, and \(0\leq\alpha<\infty\). No measure hypothesis is needed.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Rectifiability closure operations
nodes.statement_tex: Countably \(m\)-rectifiable sets are closed under taking subsets, countable unions, Lipschitz images, and modifications by \(\mathcal H^m\)-null sets.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Use subset-domain parametrizations in metric targets. For images, source and target Hausdorff measures have the same dimension \(m\).
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.
nodes.note: Several elementary declarations in one API, not a single conjunction theorem.

nodes.title: Rectifiability of the zero measure
nodes.statement_tex: The zero measure is rectifiable in every natural dimension, on every metric target with its Borel measurable structure.

nodes.title: Graphs and their subsets are rectifiable
nodes.statement_tex: Every full Lipschitz \(m\)-graph is countably \(m\)-rectifiable. Consequently every subset of such a graph is countably \(m\)-rectifiable.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Use the canonical definition by Lipschitz parametrizations on subsets of \(\mathbb R^m\); the target is Euclidean.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Borel sigma-finite carrier
nodes.statement_tex:
If \(S\subset\mathbb R^n\) is countably \(m\)-rectifiable, there exists a Borel countable union \(T\) of compact Lipschitz images such that
\[
 \mathcal H^m(S\setminus T)=0,\qquad
 \mathcal H^m\!\restriction T\text{ is sigma-finite}.
\]
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The target is Euclidean; \(m\) is a natural dimension. No measurability assumption is part of the rectifiability predicate for \(S\).
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Approximate cone criterion
Pure unrectifiability calculus
nodes.statement_tex: Every subset of a purely \(m\)-unrectifiable set is purely \(m\)-unrectifiable. Its intersection with any countably \(m\)-rectifiable set, in particular any Lipschitz \(m\)-graph, is \(\mathcal H^m\)-null.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Use the canonical pure predicate defined by testing all countably rectifiable sets.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Carrier API aggregation
nodes.statement_tex: Hausdorff-null changes of carriers preserve rectifiability of measures absolutely continuous with respect to \(\mathcal H^m\). Countably many rectifiable restrictions whose carriers cover almost all the measure assemble to a rectifiable measure.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The measure is absolutely continuous with respect to \(\mathcal H^m\). Restriction carriers are measurable and form a countable family covering the measure up to a null set.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.
nodes.note: Refines existing bundled node; declaration names for the individual elementary facts should be selected during implementation.

nodes.title: Rectifiable/pure decomposition
nodes.statement_tex:
There exist disjoint Borel sets \(R,U\subset E\) with
\[
 E=R\cup U,\qquad R\text{ countably \(m\)-rectifiable},\qquad
 U\text{ purely \(m\)-unrectifiable}.
\]
Any two such decompositions agree up to \(\mathcal H^m\)-null sets.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The set \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) is Borel and \(\mathcal H^m(E)<\infty\).
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.
nodes.note: Maximize mass among Borel canonical rectifiable subsets. Graph-only source definition is not required.

nodes.title: Positive finite density
Measure comparisons on density strata
nodes.statement_tex:
Uniform small-ball upper bounds on a Borel stratum \(S\) imply
\[
 \mu\!\restriction S\leq C\,\mathcal H^m\!\restriction S.
\]
Uniform positive lower bounds give the reverse comparison, with a finite geometric constant, and finite \(\mathcal H^m\)-measure on bounded strata.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: At every centre of \(S\), the appropriate power bound holds for all radii below one common positive cutoff. The measure is locally finite; localize to bounded strata when claiming finiteness.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.
nodes.note: Split upper and lower comparison declarations; constants may be nonoptimal but must be positive finite.

nodes.title: Dimension zero
Countable carriers
Absolute continuity with respect to zero-dimensional Hausdorff measure
Zero-dimensional density equals atomic mass
Normalization bridges
Finite upper density implies Hausdorff absolute continuity
nodes.statement_tex: If \(\Theta^{*m}(\mu,x)<\infty\) for \(\mu\)-almost every \(x\), then \(\mu\ll\mathcal H^m\).
nodes.hypotheses_tex: \(\mu\) is a locally finite Borel measure on \(\mathbb R^n\); \(m\) is a natural dimension.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Finite Hausdorff pieces with comparable measures
nodes.statement_tex:
There are bounded Borel sets \(S_j\) carrying \(\mu\), each of finite \(\mathcal H^m\)-measure, such that \(\mu\!\restriction S_j\) and \(\mathcal H^m\!\restriction S_j\) have positive finite two-sided comparison constants. In particular,
\[
 \mu\bigl((\bigcup_j S_j)^c\bigr)=0.
\]
nodes.hypotheses_tex: \(\mu\) is locally finite and \(0<\Theta_*^m(\mu,x)\leq\Theta^{*m}(\mu,x)<\infty\) for \(\mu\)-almost every \(x\).
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Dimensions above the ambient dimension
nodes.statement_tex: If $m>n$, the positive finite density hypothesis forces $\mu=0$.

nodes.title: Dimensionally normalized blow-ups
nodes.statement_tex: Set $D^m_{x,r}\mu=r^{-m}(T_{x,r})_\#\mu$, where $T_{x,r}(y)=(y-x)/r$. The definition is total in Lean; geometric theorems assume $r>0$.

nodes.title: Dimensional tangent measures
nodes.statement_tex: A nonzero regular measure $\nu$ is a dimensional tangent of $\mu$ at $x$ if $D^m_{x,r_i}\mu\rightharpoonup\nu$ for some positive sequence $r_i\to0$. This fixes the scalar normalization.

nodes.title: Tangents at infinity
nodes.statement_tex: A nonzero regular measure $\nu$ is a tangent at infinity of $\mu$ if $D^m_{0,r_i}\mu\rightharpoonup\nu$ for some positive sequence $r_i\to\infty$.

nodes.title: Flat limit excludes persistent mass away from its plane
nodes.statement_tex: If \(\nu_j\rightharpoonup c\mathcal H^m\!\restriction V\), then the mass of any fixed bounded set separated by a positive distance from \(V\) tends to zero. In particular this applies to the region outside an \(\eta\)-tube inside a fixed ball.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: All measures are regular, \(V\) is an \(m\)-plane, \(0<c<\infty\), and \(\eta>0\). Use the compact closure of the region.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Flat limit gives lower mass in moving plane balls
nodes.statement_tex:
If \(\nu_j\rightharpoonup c\mathcal H^m\!\restriction V\), then for each \(R,\eta>0\) there are \(b>0\) and \(j_0\) such that
\[
 \nu_j(B_\eta(z))\geq b
 \quad(j\geq j_0,\ z\in V\cap\overline B_R(0)).
\]
nodes.hypotheses_tex: All measures are regular, \(0<c<\infty\), and \(V\) is an \(m\)-plane. Extract converging centres and use a fixed smaller open ball.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Fixed-normalization compactness at density-bound points
nodes.statement_tex:
For every positive sequence \(r_j\to0\), there are a strictly increasing subsequence map \(\phi\) and a nonzero regular measure \(\nu\) such that
\[
 D^m_{x,r_{\phi(j)}}\mu\rightharpoonup\nu.
\]
The limit is a tangent measure in GMT's arbitrary-scalar convention.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: \(\mu\) is locally finite and \(0<\Theta_*^m(\mu,x)\leq\Theta^{*m}(\mu,x)<\infty\) at the fixed point \(x\).
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.statement_tex:
Prove
$D^m_{b,s}(D^m_{a,r}\mu)=D^m_{a+rb,rs}\mu$;
positive scalar multiplication commutes with $D$; and pushforward by a linear
isometric embedding intertwines $D$, at centres in its image. Include inverse
dilation and preservation of flatness, regularity and uniform ball constants.

dilation and preservation of flatness, regularity and uniform ball constants.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 3 and 6; general supporting analysis.

nodes.title: Support approximation from arbitrary positive outer measure sets
nodes.statement_tex:
Assume $a\in D$, $a$ is a density-one point of its measurable hull $H$,
$\limsup_{r\downarrow0}\mu(B(a,r))/r^m<\infty$, and
$D^m_{a,r_i}\mu\rightharpoonup\nu$ with $r_i\downarrow0$.
Then for every $y\in\operatorname{supp}\nu$,
$\operatorname{dist}(a+r_i y,D)/r_i\to0$.
Indeed, a subsequence of holes $B(a+r_i y,\eta r_i)$ disjoint from $D$ has
zero $H$-mass by A07. It lies in $B(a,Cr_i)$ for a fixed $C$; its remaining
mass is $o(r_i^m)$ by density-one and the upper density bound. Portmanteau
would then make $\nu(B(y,\eta))=0$, a contradiction. Choose approximate
nearest points in $D$ with error $r_i/i$; no closedness of $D$ is needed.

nodes.title: Joint continuity of translated dilations
nodes.statement_tex:
If $\mu_i\rightharpoonup\mu$, $a_i\to a$, $r_i\to r>0$, and
$c_i\to c\in[0,\infty)$, then

If every $
u_i\in\operatorname{Tan}(\mu,x)$, $
u_iightharpoonup
u$, and $
u$ is regular and nonzero, then $

nodes.title: All flat tangents imply weak linear approximation

If every tangent of \(\mathcal H^m\!\restriction F\) at \(x\) is \(m\)-flat, then \(F\) is weakly linearly approximable at \(x\):

nodes.title: Plane and scaling API

nodes.title: Positive dilations preserve dimensional tangents

nodes.title: Transitivity of the support-centered scaling orbit closure
nodes.statement_tex:
Let $\mathcal O_m(\nu)$ be the closure of
$\{D^m_{y,r}\nu:y\in\operatorname{supp}\nu,\ 0<r\leq1\}$ within regular

Blow-downs of tangents remain tangents
nodes.statement_tex:
If a dimensional tangent $\zeta$ has a nonzero regular limit at infinity $\chi$,
then $\chi$ is a dimensional tangent of the original measure at the same point.

nodes.title: Continuity of the scale function
nodes.statement_tex: For fixed regular locally finite $\mu$ and center $x$, $r\mapsto F(D^m_{x,r}\mu)$ is continuous on $(0,\infty)$.
nodes.proof_tex:
Choose $\phi\in C_c(\mathbb R^n)$ with $0\leq\phi\leq1$,
$\phi=1$ on $\overline B(0,1)$ and support in $B(0,2)$.
Define $F(\mu)=\min_V\int\phi(z)\operatorname{dist}(z,V)^2\,d\mu$.
The minimum is attained. S01 and C01 imply sequential continuity for vague
convergence; S02 implies continuity of $r\mapsto F(D^m_{x,r}\mu)$ for $r>0$.
Flat measures have $F=0$. For a unit uniform measure, $F\leq\varepsilon$
implies that some plane has unit-ball energy at most $\varepsilon$.

nodes.title: One null exceptional set for all dimensional recenterings
nodes.statement_tex:
Under positive finite existing $m$-density almost everywhere, prove
\[
 \text{for }\mu\text{-a.e. }a,\quad
 \forall\nu\in\operatorname{Tan}_m(\mu,a),\quad
 \forall y\in\operatorname{supp}\nu,\quad\forall r>0,
 \quad D^m_{y,r}\nu\in\operatorname{Tan}_m(\mu,a).
\]
Here $\operatorname{Tan}_m$ uses fixed dimensional normalization.
It is enough to prove recentering at radius one; S03 and S07 give all radii.
For fixed rational tolerances and radius cutoffs, take the arbitrary set of
bad centres, stratify its density constants and intersect with a bounded ball.
If it has positive outer measure, use a finite metric cover of the compact
family of translated uniform tangents to select one positive-outer-measure
class $D$ whose chosen translated tangents are pairwise close.
Take a density point of its measurable hull lying in $D$: the hull's bad
density points are null and cannot cover a set of positive outer measure.
Apply A08 to select nearby bad centres in $D$ and S02 to compare their blow-ups
with the chosen translated tangent. The triangle inequality contradicts the
defining fixed separation of the bad centres. Countably many tolerances give
one null exceptional set. This repairs the book's unjustified assertion that
its existentially defined set $D$ is measurable.

nodes.title: Relaxed uniform approximation good sets
nodes.statement_tex:
Let \(G(\nu,m,\eta,\lambda,R)\) consist of points \(x\) for which every \(0<r<R\) admits an \(m\)-plane \(V\) satisfying
\[
 \nu\{y:\|y-x\|<r,\ \operatorname{dist}(y-x,V)>\eta r\}\leq\eta r^m,
\]
and
\[
 \nu(\overline B_{\eta r}(z))\geq\lambda r^m
 \quad\text{for all }z\in(x+V)\cap B_r(x).
\]
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Parameters \(\eta,\lambda,R\) are positive. Later closedness results assume \(\nu\) finite and regular.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Small tube-error mass implies support containment
nodes.statement_tex:
Suppose points \(z\in C\) satisfy \(\nu(B_s(z))\geq\delta s^m\) at small scales. If the mass outside the \(\eta r/2\)-tube about \(a+V\), inside \(B_{2r}(a)\), is less than \(\delta(\eta r/2)^m\), then
\[
 C\cap B_r(a)\subset\{z:\operatorname{dist}(z,a+V)\leq\eta r\}.
\]
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The lower bounds hold uniformly at every point of \(C\), and all radii used lie below their common cutoff. Here \(\delta,\eta,r>0\).
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Weak linear approximation
nodes.statement_tex: A measure $\mu$ is weakly linearly approximable at $x$ if for every $\eta>0$ there are $a,r_0>0$ such that, for every $0<r<r_0$, some $m$-plane $V$ satisfies both $\mu(B(x,r)\setminus\{z:\operatorname{dist}(z-x,V)\leq\eta r\})<\eta r^m$ and $\mu(B(z,\eta r))\geq ar^m$ for every $z\in(x+V)\cap B(x,r)$. The set predicate specializes this to $\mathcal H^m\!\restriction E$.

nodes.title: Small projection direction bounds projected tube measure
nodes.statement_tex:
There is \(C_m>0\) such that, if \(w\in W\) is a unit vector with \(\|P_Vw\|\leq\varepsilon\), then
\[
 \mathcal H^m\!\left(P_V\bigl(\{z:\operatorname{dist}(z,a+W)\leq\eta R\}\cap\overline B_R(a)\bigr)\right)
 \leq C_m(\varepsilon+\eta)R^m.
\]
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The subspaces \(V,W\) have dimension \(m>0\); \(\varepsilon,\eta\geq0\) and \(R>0\). The constant depends only on dimension and normalization.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Relaxed approximation good sets are closed
nodes.statement_tex:
The relaxed good set \(G(\nu,m,\eta,\lambda,R)\) is closed.
For each fixed radius, the relation in \(x,V\) is closed; projection along the compact plane space and intersection over radii preserve closedness.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: \(\nu\) is finite and regular; use the compact orthogonal-projection topology on \(m\)-planes and fixed positive \(\eta,\lambda,R\).
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.
nodes.note: Prove joint LSC moving-open-set mass and USC closed-ball mass, approximate centres via projections; project closed relation along compact plane witness.

nodes.title: Weak approximation gives positive lower density
nodes.statement_tex:
Weak linear approximation of \(F\) at \(x\) implies
\[
 \Theta_*^m(\mathcal H^m\!\restriction F,x)>0.
\]
Use the lower-ball clause at the plane centre \(z=x\) and one fixed aperture.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: No finite-total-measure assumption is required for this implication. Its pure-measure version concludes a positive local lower power bound.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Weak approximation survives negligible deletion
nodes.statement_tex:
If \(F\subset E\) and
\[
 r^{-m}\mathcal H^m((E\setminus F)\cap B_{2r}(x))\longrightarrow0,
\]
then weak linear approximation of \(E\) at \(x\) implies that of \(F\) at \(x\).
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The pointwise theorem assumes the displayed limit. Shrink the source aperture and positive lower-mass constant.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Aperture slack gives countable good-set exhaustion
nodes.statement_tex:
Weak linear approximation at \(x\) implies, for every \(\eta>0\), membership in some
\(G(\nu,m,\eta,1/N,1/N)\), \(N\geq1\).
Conversely membership with aperture \(\eta/2\) gives the original approximation clauses at aperture \(\eta\).
nodes.hypotheses_tex: \(\nu=\mathcal H^m\!\restriction E\) is finite and regular. Use aperture slack to replace non-strict upper inequalities and closed lower balls by the original strict/open clauses.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Compact subsets with uniform approximation and density bounds
nodes.statement_tex: One can choose compact \(C\subset E\) losing arbitrarily little \(\mathcal H^m\)-measure, on which the selected lower mass bounds and finitely many relaxed weak-approximation conditions have uniform positive parameters.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The Borel set \(E\) has finite \(\mathcal H^m\)-measure and is weakly linearly approximable almost everywhere. Intersect Borel \(E\) with closed good sets before applying inner regularity.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Weak approximation restricts to Borel subsets almost everywhere
nodes.statement_tex: If \(E\) is weakly linearly approximable at \(\mathcal H^m\)-almost every point of \(E\), then each Borel \(F\subset E\) is weakly linearly approximable at \(\mathcal H^m\)-almost every point of \(F\).
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The set \(E\) is Borel and \(\mathcal H^m(E)<\infty\). Differentiation and finite upper density supply the negligible-deletion estimate.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Base point with upper mass and small discarded mass
nodes.statement_tex:
Choose \(a\in G\) and \(r_0>0\) so that, for \(0<r<r_0\),
\[
 \mathcal H^m(E\cap B_r(a))\leq C_m r^m,\qquad
 \mathcal H^m((E\setminus G)\cap B_{2r}(a))\leq t r^m.
\]
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The Borel sets \(G\subset E\) satisfy \(0<\mathcal H^m(G)\leq\mathcal H^m(E)<\infty\), and \(t>0\) is chosen before \(a,r_0\).
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Transfer density bounds and flat tangents to finite pieces
nodes.statement_tex:
For each finite piece \(S_j\), the measure \(
u_j=\mathcal H^m\!estriction S_j\) has positive lower and finite upper \(m\)-density almost everywhere. If all tangents of \(\mu\) are \(m\)-flat almost everywhere, the same holds for all tangents of \(
u_j\) at \(
u_j\)-almost every point.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The pieces are Borel, finite in \(\mathcal H^m\), and their restrictions are comparable with positive finite constants. Assume the density and flat-tangent hypotheses for locally finite \(\mu\).
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Nested compact two-sided approximation
nodes.statement_tex: Choose compact positive-measure sets \(G\subset F\subset E\) with uniform lower mass on \(F\). At each \(a\in G\) and each small scale \(r\), a plane \(V\) gives tube containment of \(F\cap B_{2r}(a)\), proximity of \((a+V)\cap B_r(a)\) to \(F\), and a positive lower bound for the \(E\)-mass of plane-centred \(\eta r\)-balls.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The Borel set \(E\) has positive finite \(\mathcal H^m\)-measure and is weakly linearly approximable almost everywhere. Choose the lower constant \(\delta\) first, then a sufficiently small \(\eta\), then the remaining constants.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.
nodes.note: Preserve parameter order δ then η then γ then t.

nodes.title: Pure sets have arbitrarily close points outside fixed cones
nodes.statement_tex:
For every fixed \(m\)-plane \(V\) and finite aperture \(\alpha\geq0\), at \(\mathcal H^m\)-almost every \(a\in C\), every \(r>0\) admits
\[
 b\in C\cap B_r(a)\setminus C(a,V,\alpha).
\]
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The set \(C\) is purely \(m\)-unrectifiable. The exceptional null set may depend on \(V,\alpha\); simultaneous quantification over all planes is unnecessary.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Disjoint projection-hole disks with large radius sum
nodes.statement_tex:
There is a countable family of hole centres \(p_i\) and radii \(\rho_i\) such that the disks \(D_{4\rho_i}(p_i)\) are disjoint, their fivefold enlargements cover the relevant plane disk up to a null set, and
\[
 0<\rho_i\leq\eta\sigma,\qquad \sum_i\rho_i^m\geq c_m\sigma^m.
\]
Each radius is distance to the compact projected set.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Use \(P_V(G\cap\overline B_{2\sigma}(a))\), with \(G\) compact and null projection. Plane-centred mass and the small discarded-mass bound give the upper bound on hole radii.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Pure weakly approximable sets have every-plane null projection
nodes.statement_tex:
For every \(m\)-plane \(V\),
\[
 \mathcal H^m(P_V(E))=0.
\]
This is an every-plane conclusion, not an almost-every-plane projection theorem.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The Borel set \(E\) is purely \(m\)-unrectifiable, has finite \(\mathcal H^m\)-measure, and is weakly linearly approximable almost everywhere; \(0<m\leq n\).
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.
nodes.note: Also reuse Besicovitch.exists_disjoint_closedBall_covering_ae and Lipschitz distortion; a fivefold covering alone is not identical.

nodes.title: Cylinders meeting the compact core have small radius sum
nodes.statement_tex:
For indices \(J\) whose inner cylinders meet \(F\),
\[
 \sum_{i\in J}\rho_i^m\leq C_m t\sigma^m/\delta.
\]
For sufficiently small \(t\), the complementary indices \(K\) retain
\(\sum_{i\in K}\rho_i^m\geq c_m\sigma^m\).
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Use the selected disjoint cylinders, uniform lower mass \(\delta\) on \(F\), and small mass of \(E\setminus G\). Choose \(t\) after \(\delta\).
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Many disjoint lower-mass balls inside each surviving cylinder
nodes.statement_tex: At the local scale \(r_i=\rho_i/(8\eta)\), each surviving cylinder contains at least \(c/\eta\) separated plane points and corresponding nearby centres in \(F\). The resulting balls of radius \(\rho_i/8\) are disjoint, lie inside the \(4\rho_i\)-cylinder and the ambient \(B_\sigma(a)\), and satisfy the prescribed lower mass bound.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Use an empty inner cylinder, a compact nearest projected boundary point, two-sided approximation at that point, and sufficiently small \(\eta>0\). Never identify \(\sigma\) with \(\rho_i/(8\eta)\).
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Null projections contradict weak approximation and finite upper density
nodes.statement_tex:
Summing the disjoint column balls gives
\[
 \mathcal H^m(E\cap B_\sigma(a))
 \geq c_m\delta\sigma^m/\eta,
\]
contradicting the upper bound \(C_m\sigma^m\) when \(\eta\) is sufficiently small.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Use null projections, nested compact approximation, the selected hole disks and the surviving radius sum. Parameter order is \(\delta\), then \(\eta\ll\delta\), then the other approximation constants and \(t\), and finally \(\sigma\).
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Marstrand-Mattila set criterion
nodes.statement_tex: A Borel set \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) with finite \(\mathcal H^m\)-measure which is weakly linearly approximable at \(\mathcal H^m\)-almost every point is countably \(m\)-rectifiable.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Assume \(0<m\leq n\). The zero-measure case is included and is immediate.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Marstrand-Mattila measure criterion
nodes.statement_tex:
If, at \(\mu\)-almost every \(x\),
\[
 0<\Theta_*^m(\mu,x)\leq\Theta^{*m}(\mu,x)<\infty
\]
and every tangent measure is \(m\)-flat, then \(\mu\) is \(m\)-rectifiable.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The measure \(\mu\) is locally finite and \(0<m\leq n\). Quantification over all tangents lies inside the almost-everywhere binder.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Gaussian polynomial integrability under polynomial growth
nodes.statement_tex: For a regular measure with $\mu(B(0,R))\leq C(1+R)^p$ for all $R>0$, $C,p\geq0$, every $d\in\mathbb N$ and $s>0$ satisfy $\int |z|^d e^{-s|z|^2}\,d\mu<\infty$. If $\mu\ne0$, its Gaussian mass is positive.
nodes.proof_tex:
For every $d\in\mathbb N$ and $s>0$,
$\int |z|^d e^{-s|z|^2}\,d\nu<\infty$ and $0<I_\nu(s)<\infty$.
For fixed $s,d$, the tails outside $B(0,R)$ tend to zero uniformly over
$\mathcal U_m$. State the more reusable version for a family satisfying one
common polynomial bound $\mu(B(0,R))\leq C(1+R)^p$.
Use this to extend vague convergence to polynomial-times-Gaussian tests.
It also justifies differentiation with respect to positive $s$ locally in $s$.
nodes.source: De Lellis Lemma 7.2, Definition 7.4, Lemma 7.6, Proposition 7.7, pp.70-84.

nodes.title: Analytic extension of weighted complementary projections
nodes.statement_tex:
This is a measure-independent linear algebra theorem. Let the finite-dimensional
real inner-product space $X$ have an orthogonal decomposition
$X=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{N}X_j$, with projections $P_j$, and let $V\leq X$.
For $s>0$ put $A(s)=\sum_j s^jP_j$ and
$F_s=A(s)^{-1}(V^\perp)$. Then $X=V\oplus F_s$; the projection $Q_s$
onto $V$ along $F_s$ extends real-analytically to a neighborhood of zero.
In particular its operator norm stays bounded as $s\downarrow0$.
For the proof, orthogonally split $V^\perp$ according to the filtration
$V^\perp\cap\bigoplus_{j\leq k}X_j$ and define a polynomial family which
is identity on $V$ and equals $P_k+sP_{k-1}+\cdots+s^{k-1}P_1$ on the
$k$th filtration summand. Its value at zero is invertible, by the
least-nonzero-degree argument, and $Q_s=P_V A_s^{-1}$ for that polynomial
family. In the least-degree argument the lower-degree vector belongs to the
sum of all earlier filtration summands, not necessarily only the immediately
preceding one.

nodes.title: Greatest crossing with an interval bound
nodes.statement_tex: If $0<a<b$, $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and $f(a)>\varepsilon>f(b)$, there is $c\in(a,b)$ such that $f(c)=\varepsilon$ and $f(t)\leq\varepsilon$ for all $t\in[c,b]$.
nodes.proof_tex:
After S08 normalization, suppose $\alpha$ is a flat dimensional tangent and
$\zeta$ is a nonflat dimensional tangent, all dimensional tangents being unit

and $s_i<r_i$ with blow-ups tending to $\chi$; subsequence selection makes

at most $\varepsilon$ on the entire interval $[\sigma_i,r_i]$.

nodes.title: Gaussian weighted polynomials determine growing measures
nodes.statement_tex:
Regular measures with a common polynomial growth bound are equal if their
$e^{-|z|^2}$-weighted polynomial moments agree. One rigorous route extends

exponential series, then iterates to all positive integer rates.
The algebra generated by constants and $e^{-k|z|^2}P(z)$, $k\geq1$, extends
continuously to the one-point compactification and separates points.
Stone--Weierstrass approximates $e^{|z|^2}\varphi$ uniformly for compactly
supported $\varphi$; multiply by $e^{-|z|^2}$ and use Gaussian integrability.
Expanding $e^{-a|z|^2}$ under an integral at arbitrary $a$ in one step is not
justified by absolute domination, so that step in the book needs this repair
or a separate uniqueness theorem with checked exponential-moment hypotheses.

nodes.title: Uniform Gaussian polynomial tails

$\int\langle y,v\rangle^2\langle z,v\rangle^2\,d\gamma
=|y|^2|z|^2+2\langle y,z\rangle^2$.
Combining this with R07 yields, for $w\in V^\perp$,
\[

nodes.title: Approximation of support points under vague convergence
nodes.statement_tex: If regular $\mu_i\rightharpoonup\mu$ and $x\in\operatorname{supp}\mu$, there are, for all sufficiently large $i$, $x_i\in\operatorname{supp}\mu_i$ with $x_i\to x$.

If regular $\mu_i\rightharpoonup\mu$ and $x\in\operatorname{supp}\mu$, then
there exist $x_i\in\operatorname{supp}\mu_i$ with $x_i\to x$, after discarding

have a common positive lower support-centred ball bound at each radius, then
$x\in\operatorname{supp}\mu$. Bare vague convergence does not give this converse.

\[

 \geq(1+2/m)\left(\int A(v,v)\,d\gamma\right)^2.
\]

$|b_{k,s}(u_1,\ldots,u_k)|\leq
C_m 2^k k^{k/2}s^{k/2}\prod_i|u_i|/k!$.

$\sum_{k\geq0} b_{k,s}(x^k)=e^{s|x|^2}$ follows by translating the

 \leq C_{m,q}(s|x|^2)^{q+1/2}.
\]

nodes.title: Comparison of homogeneous ball and Gaussian energies
nodes.statement_tex:

u$ is $m$-homogeneous and $h\geq0$ is measurable and $a$-homogeneous with $m+a>0$ and finite unit-ball integral, then $\int e^{-|z|^2}h(z)\,d
u=\Gamma((m+a)/2+1)\int_{B(0,1)}h(z)\,d
u$. In particular $h(z)=\operatorname{dist}(z,V)^2$ gives the constant $\Gamma(m/2+2)$.

For every plane $V$, the distance-squared measure has homogeneous degree
$m+2$, so
$\int e^{-|z|^2}\operatorname{dist}(z,V)^2\,d\nu
=C_m\int_{B(0,1)}\operatorname{dist}(z,V)^2\,d\nu$
for a finite positive constant $C_m$ obtained by radial integration.

nodes.title: Absolutely convergent Gaussian translation series

Prove the norm bound
$|b_{k,s}(u_1,\ldots,u_k)|\leq
C_m 2^k k^{k/2}s^{k/2}\prod_i|u_i|/k!$.
For $x$ in the support, the absolutely convergent series
$\sum_{k\geq0} b_{k,s}(x^k)=e^{s|x|^2}$ follows by translating the
Gaussian. A valid dominating function is
$e^{-s|z|^2+2s|z||x|}$, bounded by a constant times
$e^{-(s/2)|z|^2}$, not the expression with a negative cross term printed in

\[
 \left|\sum_{k=1}^{2q}b_{k,s}(x^k)
 -\sum_{j=1}^{q}\frac{s^j|x|^{2j}}{j!}\right|
 \leq C_{m,q}(s|x|^2)^{q+1/2}.
\]

the convergent exponential series with its remainder bound.

\[

\]

nodes.title: Elementary eigenvalue rigidity from one nearby support point
nodes.statement_tex: For a PSD form $B$ of trace $m$, a support set satisfying $B(x,x)=|x|^2$, and an ordered orthonormal eigenbasis, suppose there is a support point within $\delta$ of the $m$th eigenvector, $0<\delta<1/m$. If $\alpha_m<1$, the trace gives
$\alpha_i-1\leq(m-1)(1-\alpha_m)$ for $i<m$ and
$\alpha_i\leq\alpha_m$ for $i\geq m$.
The support identity then gives
$0\leq(1-\alpha_m)((m-1)^2\delta^2-(1-\delta)^2)<0$.
Thus $\alpha_m\geq1$. Trace $m$ forces the first $m$ eigenvalues to be one
and the rest zero. Hence support is contained in $V$ and $\nu=\sigma_V$.

two-dimensional shortcut in the original printed proof.

nodes.title: Even Taylor coefficients from a flat blow-down

nodes.title: Odd top coefficients vanish on the flat limiting plane

nodes.title: Cylinder identity and bounded normal coordinates

nodes.title: Mixed Gaussian moment limit defining omega
nodes.statement_tex: For all ambient $v,w$, $\lim_{s\downarrow0}\frac{8s}{I(s)}\int e^{-s|z|^2}\langle z,v\rangle^2\langle z-b,w\rangle\,d\nu=3b_3^{(2)}(v,v,w)-4b_2^{(1)}(v,v)\langle b,w\rangle$. For $v\in V,w\in V^\perp$ this equals $\langle\omega(v,v),w\rangle$.
nodes.proof_tex:
For $v,w\in\mathbb R^n$, prove
\[
 \lim_{s\downarrow0}\frac{8s}{I(s)}\int e^{-s|z|^2}
 \langle z,v\rangle^2\langle z-b,w\rangle\,d\nu
 =3b_3^{(2)}(v,v,w)-4b_2^{(1)}(v,v)\langle b,w\rangle.
\]
For $v\in V,w\in V^\perp$ this is $\langle\omega(v,v),w\rangle$.

\[

 |Pz|^2\langle z-b,w\rangle\,d\nu=0.
\]

nodes.source: De Lellis Proposition 9.1, Lemmas 9.2,9.4,9.9,9.10 and Proposition 9.5, pp.95-109.

nodes.title: Normal second Taylor trace
nodes.proof_tex:
The exact radial identity $\operatorname{tr}b_{2,s}=ms$ and M07 imply
$\operatorname{tr}b_2^{(2)}=0$.
R03 and the first-moment expansion give
$\operatorname{tr}(b_2^{(2)}|V^\perp)=8|b|^2
=2\|b_1^{(1)}\|^2$.

nodes.source: De Lellis Proposition 9.1, Lemmas 9.2,9.4,9.9,9.10 and Proposition 9.5, pp.95-109.

nodes.title: Bounded distance from the limiting plane to the support

There exists $R_0<\infty$ with
$\operatorname{dist}(v,\operatorname{supp}\nu)<R_0$ for every $v\in V$.

S05 gives a unit uniform limit supported in $V$, hence $\sigma_V$.
The original holes give a unit hole centred at a bounded point of $V$, a
contradiction. The centres $z_i$ need not lie in the support, which is why the
near-support variant of S05 is essential.

nodes.source: De Lellis Proposition 9.1, Lemmas 9.2,9.4,9.9,9.10 and Proposition 9.5, pp.95-109.

nodes.title: Zero Gaussian mean of omega
nodes.statement_tex: For standard covariance-one Gaussian probability $\gamma_V$ on $V$, $\int\omega(v,v)\,d\gamma_V(v)=0$. Equivalently its inner product with every fixed normal vector has integral zero.
nodes.proof_tex:
Let $\gamma$ be the standard covariance-one Gaussian probability measure on
$V$. Prove $\int\langle\omega(v,v),b\rangle\,d\gamma(v)=0$ using R07,
Fubini and domination by a constant times $|v|^2$.
Then
$\operatorname{tr}(b_2^{(2)}|V)=\int\widehat b(v,v)\,d\gamma(v)$.
The same argument works against each fixed normal vector, not only $b$.

nodes.title: Pointwise square bound for the adjusted form
nodes.statement_tex:
For all $v\in V$,
$\widehat b(v,v)^2\leq |b|^2|\omega(v,v)|^2$.
Choose support points $t_i v+v_i+w_i$ within bounded distance of $t_i v$ using
R05. Pass to a convergent subsequence of bounded normal components $w_i$.
Divide R09 by $t_i^2$ and use R03 to obtain
$b_2^{(2)}(v,v)+\langle\omega(v,v),w\rangle=0$ and
$|w|^2=2\langle b,w\rangle$.
Thus $|w-b|=|b|$ and
$\widehat b(v,v)+\langle\omega(v,v),w-b\rangle=0$; Cauchy--Schwarz proves
the inequality.

Hence its integral against $sI(s)^{-1}e^{-s|z|^2}\nu$ tends to zero.
This is equation (9.34); it is a necessary bridge to the global trace bound.

nodes.title: Gaussian reproducing identity for omega
nodes.statement_tex: For $y\in V,w\in V^\perp$, $\int\langle y,v\rangle^2\langle\omega(v,v),w\rangle\,d\gamma_V(v)=2\langle\omega(y,y),w\rangle$.

$\int\langle y,v\rangle^2\langle z,v\rangle^2\,d\gamma

Combining this with R07 yields, for $w\in V^\perp$,
\[
 \int\langle y,v\rangle^2\langle\omega(v,v),w\rangle\,d\gamma(v)
 =2\langle\omega(y,y),w\rangle.
\]
Justify limits by Gaussian quartic domination and Fubini.
nodes.source: De Lellis Proposition 9.1, Lemmas 9.2,9.4,9.9,9.10 and Proposition 9.5, pp.95-109.

\[
 \int\widehat b(v,v)^2\,d\gamma(v)
 \leq-8|b|^2\int\widehat b(v,v)\,d\gamma(v).
\]
The inequality must remain an inequality throughout. The equality sign at
the start of the second long display on printed page 108 loses the earlier
inequality; its final statement (9.41) has the correct direction.

nodes.title: Positive lower bound for the total second coefficient trace
nodes.statement_tex: For a unit uniform measure with flat blow-down, $\operatorname{tr}b_2^{(2)}\geq16|b|^2/(m+2)$. More precisely $\int\widehat b(v,v)\,d\gamma_V\geq-8m|b|^2/(m+2)$.

For every symmetric bilinear form $A$ on an $m$-dimensional Euclidean space,
\[
 \int A(v,v)^2\,d\gamma=(\operatorname{tr}A)^2+
 2\|A\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2
 \geq(1+2/m)\left(\int A(v,v)\,d\gamma\right)^2.
\]
This is a reusable Gaussian/spectral theorem independent of uniform measures.
Combining it with R13 gives
$\int\widehat b(v,v)\,d\gamma\geq-8m|b|^2/(m+2)$.
R08 and R04 therefore give
$\operatorname{tr}b_2^{(2)}\geq16|b|^2/(m+2)$.
Since that trace is zero, $b=0$; R03 makes the support planar, and plane-supported
uniform classification finishes rigidity. This is the actual content hidden
inside the current single trace-rigidity node.

nodes.statement_tex:
Intersect the a.e. sets for uniformity, density and A09. Choose any tangent,
use A06, recenter every approximating term using A09, and use S07 for the
nonzero flat limit. This is \texttt{ae\_exists\_flat\_tangent}.

nodes.title: First-crossing sequences and their uniform tangent limit
nodes.statement_tex:
After S08 normalization, suppose $\alpha$ is a flat dimensional tangent and
$\zeta$ is a nonflat dimensional tangent, all dimensional tangents being unit
uniform. Let $\chi$ be the blow-down of $\zeta$. Rigidity and the gap give
$F(\chi)>\varepsilon$. Choose $r_i\to0$ with blow-ups tending to $\alpha$
and $s_i<r_i$ with blow-ups tending to $\chi$; subsequence selection makes
the ordering possible. For sufficiently large $i$, the continuous scale
function satisfies $F(D_{x,r_i}^m\mu)<\varepsilon$ and
$F(D_{x,s_i}^m\mu)>\varepsilon$.
Choose $\sigma_i\in[s_i,r_i]$ with energy exactly $\varepsilon$ and energy
at most $\varepsilon$ on the entire interval $[\sigma_i,r_i]$.
This is a greatest-crossing/last-crossing assertion, not merely the intermediate
value theorem. Extract a nonzero unit uniform limit $\xi$ at the $\sigma_i$.

nodes.title: Preiss
Lipschitz maps take null domain sets to Hausdorff-null sets
nodes.statement_tex: If \(f:A\to\mathbb R^n\) is Lipschitz and \(\mathcal L^m(A)=0\), then \(\mathcal H^m(f(A))=0\).
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Here \(A\subset\mathbb R^m\). Use the Hausdorff/Lebesgue normalization on the domain and Lipschitz distortion.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Affine graph area formula
nodes.statement_tex: For an injective affine graph parametrization, pushforward of its Jacobian-weighted source Haar measure equals Hausdorff measure on the affine graph, with the fixed normalization factor.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The spaces are finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces and the affine linear part is injective. State an equality of measures, hence a formula on every Borel restriction.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Graphs are closed with finite bounded measure
nodes.statement_tex:
Every full Lipschitz \(m\)-graph \(\Gamma\) is closed, and
\[
 \mathcal H^m(\Gamma\cap\overline B_R(x))<\infty
\]
for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and finite radius \(R\).
nodes.hypotheses_tex: \(\Gamma=\{v+f(v):v\in V\}\), where \(\dim V=m\) and \(f:V\to V^\perp\) is Lipschitz.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Full-rank differentiability locus maps into countably many graphs
nodes.statement_tex: The image of the full-rank differentiability locus of a Lipschitz \(f:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n\) is covered by countably many full Lipschitz \(m\)-graphs.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Use countable derivative-control pieces and a countable family of approximating full-rank matrices. For a nonempty rank-\(m\) locus, \(m\leq n\).
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Rank-deficient derivative image is null
nodes.statement_tex: For a Lipschitz \(f:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n\), the image of its differentiability locus where \(\operatorname{rank}(Df)<m\) is \(\mathcal H^m\)-null.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Work with measurable pieces or suitable measurable envelopes. This is the rank-deficient-image lemma, not an invocation of an already available full area formula.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.
nodes.note: De Lellis Lemma4.11; do not claim the full area formula already exists.

nodes.title: Area formula for Lipschitz graph parametrizations
nodes.statement_tex: For a Lipschitz graph parametrization \(F(v)=v+f(v)\), Hausdorff measure on its graph is the pushforward of the measurable Jacobian-weighted domain measure, with the normalization established in the affine case.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Define the Jacobian on the differentiability locus and choose a measurable extension on its null complement. The map \(F\) is injective.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Fixed-dimensional blow-up transfer under density change
nodes.statement_tex:
If \(\lambda=f\mu\), then at good differentiation points \(x\), for every compactly supported continuous \(\varphi\),
\[
 \int\varphi\,dD^m_{x,r}\lambda-
 f(x)\int\varphi\,dD^m_{x,r}\mu\longrightarrow0.
\]
The exact multiplier \(f(x)\) is retained.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The measures are locally finite; \(f\geq0\) is locally \(\mu\)-integrable; \(x\) is a differentiation point and has finite upper \(m\)-density for \(\mu\).
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.
nodes.note: Reuse GMT MatchingTangents norm_integral_cc_le, weaklyConverges_of_tendsto_integral_sub, tendsto_mul_measure_diff_zero. Finite upper density addresses author erratum for Prop3.12.

nodes.title: Lipschitz-image and graph rectifiability agree
nodes.statement_tex:
A set \(S\subset\mathbb R^n\) is countably \(m\)-rectifiable if and only if there is a countable family of full Lipschitz \(m\)-graphs \(\Gamma_j\) such that
\[
 \mathcal H^m(S\setminus\bigcup_j\Gamma_j)=0.
\]
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Natural dimensions \(m,n\) are arbitrary. For \(m>n\), use \(\mathcal H^m(\mathbb R^n)=0\) and the empty graph family. Measurability is not intrinsic to this set predicate.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Blow-ups of graph measure converge to its derivative plane
nodes.statement_tex:
For \(\mathcal H^m\)-almost every \(x\) of a full Lipschitz graph \(\Gamma\), one plane \(V_x\) satisfies
\[
 D^m_{x,r}(\mathcal H^m\!\restriction\Gamma)
 \rightharpoonup\mathcal H^m\!\restriction V_x
 \quad(r\downarrow0).
\]
nodes.hypotheses_tex: Assume \(m>0\). Local finiteness follows from the graph measure API. Choose \(V_x\) before quantifying over positive sequences of radii.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Density representation on a sigma-finite carrier
nodes.statement_tex:
The measure \(\mu\) is \(m\)-rectifiable if and only if
\[
 \mu=(\mathcal H^m\!\restriction S)\mathbin{\mathrm{withDensity}} f
\]
for a Borel countably \(m\)-rectifiable set \(S\), a sigma-finite restriction \(\mathcal H^m\!\restriction S\), and a measurable \(f:\mathbb R^n\to[0,\infty]\).
nodes.hypotheses_tex: \(\mu\) is locally finite. Radon--Nikodym is applied on the carrier restriction, not on ambient \(\mathcal H^m\) when \(m<n\).
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Rectifiable measures have a single normalized flat limit
nodes.statement_tex:
At \(\mu\)-almost every \(x\) there exist one \(m\)-plane \(V_x\) and one \(0<c_x<\infty\) such that
\[
 D^m_{x,r}\mu\rightharpoonup c_x\mathcal H^m\!\restriction V_x
 \quad(r\downarrow0).
\]
The same \(V_x,c_x\) work for every positive sequence \(r_j\to0\).
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The measure \(\mu\) is locally finite and \(m\)-rectifiable, with \(0<m\leq n\).
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Rectifiable density and common tangent plane
nodes.statement_tex:
At \(\mu\)-almost every \(x\), the \(m\)-density exists and is positive and finite, and there is one \(m\)-plane \(V_x\) such that
\[
 \operatorname{Tan}(\mu,x)
 =\{c\,\mathcal H^m\!\restriction V_x:0<c<\infty\}.
\]
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The measure \(\mu\) is locally finite and \(m\)-rectifiable, with \(0<m\leq n\). Tangents use GMT's arbitrary positive scalar normalization.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Full tangent characterization
nodes.statement_tex: The measure \(\mu\) is \(m\)-rectifiable if and only if positive lower and finite upper \(m\)-density hold almost everywhere and every tangent is \(m\)-flat almost everywhere. On the right, the plane may depend on the individual tangent; rectifiability subsequently supplies a common plane almost everywhere.
nodes.hypotheses_tex: The measure \(\mu\) is locally finite and \(0<m\leq n\). No density-limit existence or common-plane hypothesis is assumed on the right.
nodes.source: De Lellis Chapters 4--5; see the rectifiability audit.

nodes.title: Permutation symmetry of Gaussian moment forms
nodes.statement_tex: Gaussian moment forms are invariant under every permutation of their arguments. The total Bochner definition is symmetric even when a nonintegrable kernel has integral zero.

nodes.title: A common polynomial growth bound
nodes.statement_tex: A common polynomial growth bound consists of finite real constants $C,p\geq0$ such that $\mu(\overline B(0,R))\leq C(1+R)^p$ for every $R>0$.

nodes.title: An admissible flatness cutoff
nodes.statement_tex: A cutoff $\phi\in C_c(\mathbb R^n,\mathbb R)$ is admissible when $0\leq\phi\leq1$, it equals one on the closed unit ball, and its topological support lies in the open ball of radius two.

nodes.title: Existence of an admissible cutoff
nodes.statement_tex: An admissible flatness cutoff exists in every Euclidean dimension.

nodes.title: A cutoff flatness gap threshold
nodes.statement_tex: A positive number $\varepsilon$ is a cutoff gap threshold if every unit $m$-uniform conical measure with cutoff flatness at most $\varepsilon$ is flat.

nodes.title: Transfer the conical gap to cutoff flatness
nodes.statement_tex: For $0<m\leq n$ and an admissible cutoff, there exists a positive cutoff gap threshold.

nodes.title: Quantified crossing scale data
nodes.statement_tex: Crossing data record positive scales $\sigma_i\leq r_i\to0$, vague limits of the two blow-up sequences, energy exactly $\varepsilon$ at every $\sigma_i$ and at its limit, and energy at most $\varepsilon$ on every interval $[\sigma_i,r_i]$. Divergence of $r_i/\sigma_i$ and flatness at infinity are separate conclusions.

nodes.title: Existence of the normal first-moment vector
nodes.statement_tex: For a unit uniform measure with a flat blow-down on $V$ and an explicit moment expansion, there exists $b\in V^\perp$ representing the first Taylor coefficient: $B_1^{(1)}(x)=2\langle b,x\rangle$.

nodes.title: Existence of the rigidity bilinear forms
nodes.statement_tex: Given the moment expansion, flat blow-down plane, and normal first-moment vector, there exist the normal-valued symmetric bilinear form $\omega$ and adjusted real symmetric bilinear form satisfying their exact defining identities.

nodes.title: Inner products and grading of polynomial features
nodes.statement_tex: The coordinate polynomial feature map recovers the weighted powers of $\langle x,y\rangle$ through inner products. Its homogeneous coordinate blocks form an orthogonal grading.

nodes.title: Uniform measures with a specified ball constant
nodes.statement_tex: An uncentered uniform measure with constant $q$ is regular, has nonempty support, satisfies $q>0$, and gives every closed support-centered ball of radius $r>0$ mass $qr^m$. Nonempty support excludes the zero measure.

nodes.title: Centered unit normalization
nodes.statement_tex: A measure is unit uniform exactly when it is uniform with constant one and its support contains the origin.

nodes.title: Scaling uniform measures and their ball constants
nodes.statement_tex: Dimensional blow-ups preserve a specified uniform ball constant. Centering at a support point preserves unit uniformity. Multiplication by a positive finite scalar multiplies the ball constant by the same scalar.

nodes.title: Values of existing dimensional densities
nodes.statement_tex: For an outer measure on a pseudo extended metric space and any real dimension parameter, convergence of the dimensional density ratio identifies its density value with the limit. Whenever the density exists, its value equals both the lower and upper densities.
